cover.imageDescription: Stephen stands in an ordinary night city while a vast blue-white and gold psychic membrane hangs beyond him. Small scenes of listening, work and relationship are linked by fine gold lines beneath the title THE LOCK.
cover.transcript:
TONE COMICS
THE LOCK
SOME DOORS OPEN ONLY WHEN FORGETTING STOPS.
GOOOOONG

page-01.imageDescription: Stephen appears as a child, adolescent and adult beneath an immense indigo night sky. Ordinary life continues while an unnamed longing remains.
page-01.transcript:
There was always something else.
Not a plan. Not a voice. Not even a belief.
Just the ache that ordinary life couldn’t quite be the whole story.
MOOOOORE.

page-02.imageDescription: A diagonal montage follows young Stephen through travel, university difficulty, a plain meditation centre and a quiet retreat, ending with him calmly overlooking a city.
page-02.transcript:
My life rarely arrived as a map.
A door appeared.
I walked through.
Then another.

page-03.imageDescription: In warm domestic and learning spaces, Stephen makes coffee, listens closely, explains something and helps another person settle before sharing a small smile.
page-03.transcript:
I never became the man with the grand mission.
Mostly, I listened.
Explained.
Helped things settle.

page-04.imageDescription: At night, Stephen closes his eyes and meets a translucent blue-white membrane around his forehead. He reaches toward it, but it remains quiet and intact.
page-04.transcript:
Then there was the block.
Not fear exactly.
More like an invisible wall that cancelled momentum.
What the hell is that?

page-05.imageDescription: Stephen searches through crowded late-night screens about volunteers, Pleiades, veils and grounding, reacting with doubt and reluctant recognition.
page-05.transcript:
Then the internet became very normal.
volunteer / Pleiades / veil / hold the light / grounded antenna
Yeah, sure. Pleiadian starseed. Completely reasonable.
Annoyingly, some of it pressed exactly the right buttons.

page-06.imageDescription: Stephen sits quietly before the blue-white membrane as crowded thoughts recede. A few spare questions and answers occupy increasing negative space.
page-06.transcript:
Is there actually a lock?
yes.
Why?
to keep you grounded.

page-07.imageDescription: A close view of Stephen asking for change opens into a montage of breakfast, traffic, work, family, rain, irritation, help and laughter.
page-07.transcript:
What needs to happen before the lock changes?
life.
…Helpful.

page-08.imageDescription: Three quiet panels show Stephen asking what matters now, followed by a wide image in which the same room is seen as a single connected field.
page-08.transcript:
What am I supposed to understand right now?
view.
That one landed differently.

page-09.imageDescription: Tight, pressured panels of physical sensation and worry open into a broad release as a circular resonance ripple turns Stephen’s attention.
page-09.transcript:
Under pressure, I forgot everything complicated.
But one thing survived.
GOOOOONG
And attention turned.

page-10.imageDescription: Stephen’s seeing, hearing, throat, thoughts and surrounding space participate in one luminous oscillating field, shown through a central image and small sensory insets.
page-10.transcript:
Waveform.
Seeing. Hearing. Throat. Thought. Space. All at once.
Then even the word wasn’t needed.

page-11.imageDescription: Bodily discomfort, thoughts, the room and the observing story soften into one borderless radiant display without erasing any part.
page-11.transcript:
The throat could simply be a throat.
Thought could think.
Even the story about getting free was part of the display.
Nothing had to be thrown out first.

page-12.imageDescription: Relief arrives, then Stephen tries to hold it. Panels tighten around his effort until the familiar central observer returns.
page-12.transcript:
Then relief arrived.
So naturally…
Keep this.
And there I was again.

page-13.imageDescription: Moments of pressure, recognition, relief, grasping, forgetting and ordinary life circle a small warm-gold centre in a subtle spiral.
page-13.transcript:
Forget.
Remember.
Forget again.
Not a straight path.
A spiral.

page-14.imageDescription: A distressed person arrives amid visual noise. Stephen listens, the conversation clarifies and both people leave with a little more room.
page-14.transcript:
Long before the mythology, there was a simpler pattern.
Some conversations began tangled.
Sometimes we left with a little more room.
Ambient stabiliser.

page-15.imageDescription: Stephen stands normally on a tram platform or city footpath while a barely visible vertical blue-white and gold line connects sky, body and ground.
page-15.transcript:
Grounded antenna.
Maybe grounding wasn’t blocking what I noticed.
Maybe it was what made it useful.

page-16.imageDescription: Across several close conversations, Stephen mostly listens. Each other person visibly keeps their agency and gains room to breathe.
page-16.transcript:
Maybe sanctuary isn’t somewhere you go.
Maybe sometimes it’s the few minutes another person doesn’t have to defend themselves.

page-17.imageDescription: Stephen moves through agitation, calm, humour and quiet presence as the pattern of relationships around him changes subtly with each state.
page-17.transcript:
Every state affects a room.
Agitation does.
Care does.
The question was never whether my state took part.
Only how.

page-18.imageDescription: Stephen bridges family life, student work, contemplative reading and ordinary humour through several linked rooms without becoming their centre.
page-18.transcript:
Connector.
Not because I knew the final truth.
Because I could sometimes keep two worlds in the same room.

page-19.imageDescription: On an ordinary crossing, faint echoes of listening, sanctuary, grounding and connection gather into one quiet role while Stephen remains human and slightly amused.
page-19.transcript:
Different language. Same shape.
Coherence keeper.
Ridiculous.
Still… it fit better than ambition ever had.

page-20.imageDescription: Stephen faces the Lock and strains to see beyond it while, behind him, small ordinary scenes show people settling, reconnecting and thinking clearly.
page-20.transcript:
I kept staring at what I couldn’t access.
And almost missed what was already happening.

page-21.imageDescription: In a dreamlike threshold, distant nonhuman silhouettes and impossible architecture remain ambiguous while tiny workaday details undercut the grandeur.
page-21.transcript:
What if the feeling was older than the story I had about it?
What if ‘volunteer’ was less a memory than a shape the longing recognised?

page-22.imageDescription: A luminous figure descends through layers of identity, memory and context until Stephen appears fully ordinary, newborn and human.
page-22.transcript:
Maybe coming all the way in meant forgetting enough to become ordinary.
Not pretending to be human.
Being human.

page-23.imageDescription: Stephen resists a simple answer, but scenes of work, relationship and responsibility show the translucent membrane repeatedly returning him to ordinary life.
page-23.transcript:
What if doubt wasn’t a flaw in the system?
What if some uncertainty kept this ordinary life intact?
I kept returning to the phrase: ‘to keep you grounded.’

page-24.imageDescription: A night sky, gooseflesh, softened expression and faint familiar tune suggest recognition without a literal memory or proof.
page-24.transcript:
No memory.
No coordinates.
No proof.
And still… recognition.
Like remembering the shape of a song you can’t quite hear.

page-25.imageDescription: Stephen imagines a cosmic roster punctured by two tiny office-like details. His thoughtful expression gives way to a brief, affectionate joke.
page-25.transcript:
Apparently I wasn’t the only cosmic contractor unhappy with the roster.
The backpay better be enormous.
PENDING.

page-26.imageDescription: Stephen stops trying to force an answer and responds to one ordinary next thing at a time: a walk, a message, a helping hand, a changed direction and rest.
page-26.transcript:
Less conquest.
Less demanding the whole map.
A little more give.
Life presented the next thing.
I answered.

page-27.imageDescription: The familiar Lock returns during a difficult day. Stephen notices discomfort and the urge to force it, then meets it with an open hand.
page-27.transcript:
The lock stayed.
So did the old urge to force it.
But the relationship had changed.

page-28.imageDescription: A single resonance ripple passes through Stephen, the Lock, body sensations, thoughts and starfield until the membrane becomes transparent within the whole field.
page-28.transcript:
GOOOOONG
View.
Waveform.
Then nothing needed naming.

page-29.imageDescription: Stephen looks through the now-transparent Lock. Stars and impossible forms remain hints rather than answers, and he responds with a small human smile.
page-29.transcript:
I still didn’t know where I came from.
I still didn’t know what any of it meant.
But the not-knowing had stopped being a wall.
Recognition was enough for now.

page-30.imageDescription: Morning returns Stephen to coffee, work, relationships and the next practical step. A small resonance ripple appears and passes as he walks into ordinary life.
page-30.transcript:
The answer had been annoyingly accurate.
Life.
The lock remained. The wall didn’t.
